articles.headline: Letter from Mr. Birney -- the Ohio Anti-Slavery Society
articles.author: James G. Birney
articles.summary: Letter from James G. Birney (addressed to Brother Leavitt) reporting the meeting of the Ohio Anti-Slavery Society, held in the Rev. Wm. Butcher's meeting house, with the Hon. Leicester King presiding as President. Birney describes the western anti-slavery movement's growth and the character of the deliberations, and touches on the Indiana state society.

articles.headline: New England Anti-Slavery Convention -- Sixth Annual Meeting (proceedings)
articles.summary: Report of the proceedings of the Sixth New England Anti-Slavery Convention, assembled at the Chardon Street Chapel, Boston, on May 28, 1839, pursuant to a call signed by the officers of the several New England state A. S. societies. Called to order by Wendell Phillips; Nathaniel B. Borden of Fall River elected President and Wm. Bassett of Lynn Secretary pro tem; permanent officers and committees then elected. A resolution restricting membership to gentlemen (offered as a substitute by Amos A. Phelps) was rejected and Wendell Phillips's open-membership resolution adopted after debate.

events.name: Sixth New England Anti-Slavery Convention
events.description: Sixth annual New England Anti-Slavery Convention, Chardon Street Chapel, Boston, opening May 28, 1839. Nathaniel B. Borden of Fall River was elected President, with vice-presidents from each New England state and a business committee of leading abolitionists including William Lloyd Garrison, Wendell Phillips and Maria W. Chapman. The Pennsylvania agents C. C. Burleigh (business committee) and Wm. M. Chase (secretary) took part. Reported in the Pennsylvania Freeman of June 6, 1839.
